title: How MCP connects agents to your tools

creative_direction.core_message: MCP gives an agent a standard way to reach tools and data: host, client, server, JSON-RPC.
creative_direction.viewer_benefit: Understand what happens when you add an MCP server.
creative_direction.hook: Your AI agent only knows the tools you plug in.
creative_direction.sound_design: impact on hook, ticks, chime on CTA

claims.text: MCP uses a client-server architecture: a host application creates one MCP client per MCP server.
MCP servers expose tools, resources and prompts.
Local servers commonly use the stdio transport; remote servers use Streamable HTTP.

scenes.narration: Your AI agent only knows the tools you plug in. MCP is the plug.
scenes.heading: MCP is how agents get tools

scenes.narration: The host app, like Claude Code, creates one MCP client for every server it connects to.
scenes.heading: One client per server

scenes.narration: Each server exposes three things: tools to call, resources to read, and prompts to reuse.
scenes.heading: Tools, resources, prompts

steps: Tools: actions the model can call

scenes.narration: Under the hood, every request is a JSON-RPC message: a method, parameters, and an ID.
scenes.heading: It's just JSON-RPC

scenes.narration: Local servers usually talk over standard input and output. Remote servers use streamable HTTP.
scenes.heading: Two transports

scenes.narration: One rule: only connect servers you trust, because their tools act with your permissions.
scenes.heading: Only trust servers you'd run

scenes.narration: Want the setup guide? Comment GUIDE.
scenes.heading: Comment GUIDE
